record.summary: Illinois law on the developers of the largest advanced AI systems, signed on 6 July 2026 and taking effect on 1 January 2027. It requires them to publicly disclose their safety practices, report significant safety incidents, maintain compliance processes and undergo regular independent third-party safety audits of covered systems by qualified experts without financial conflicts of interest. It also creates confidential reporting channels and whistleblower protections for employees who raise AI safety concerns.
record.notes: Sponsored by Senator Mary Edly-Allen and Representative Daniel Didech and passed with bipartisan support. It builds on the frameworks California and New York had already passed (SB 53 and the RAISE Act, US-CA-05 and US-NY-01) and adds mandatory independent third-party audits.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Governor's press release of 6 Jul 2026 on the State of Illinois Newsroom (gov-pritzker-newsroom.prezly.com, listed as the Governor's official newsroom), stored 11 Oct 2026. The copy stored on 11 Oct 2026 is a Prezly preview with a temporary URL; the published release at its permanent URL was stored in this run (same text, without the preview banner), and official_url now points at it. The release confirms the bill number, the act's name, the signing on 6 Jul 2026, passage by the General Assembly, the 1 Jan 2027 effective date, the core obligations and the sponsors. It gives no Public Act number, thresholds (revenue, compute), penalties or enforcing authority; the earlier note's thresholds rested on a law-firm summary and press reports, and those sentences were moved out of the notes. The '104th General Assembly' in official_identifier is not shown in the stored file. The enrolled text and the bill-status page on ilga.gov were not stored: ilga.gov refused connections in this run, as it did before.
